![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/7eb8812e90e4862a3658773186fe3809b212d58d5d22613fac6d9067ae4ccbc9.png)

The region enclosed by the curve $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x,$ the vertical line $x=e,$ and the horizontal line $y=0$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $x=e,$ as shown in the picture. Which of the following integrals gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.worked_solution:
Since our region rotates about a vertical line, we need to write the equation of the given curve in terms of $y:$ 

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,⟹\,x={e}^{y}
$$

 

Also, notice that the limits of integration are from $y=0$ to $y=1$ along the $y$-axis.

To determine which is the left and which is the right function, let's draw our horizontal arrow.  

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/f0ddb5b21bdff9cbed426abed5bf9b94c4c4c4d742e2eb90dcdb92895c2adf3a.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the left function $x={e}^{y},$ and

- *leaves* through the right function $x=e.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(\text{right function})-(\text{left function})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[\,(e)-({e}^{y})\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}(e-{e}^{y})^{2}\,\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{2y}-2{e}^{y+1}+{e}^{2})\,\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
